# Chat Model

This file defines the Mongoose schemas and models for managing real-time chat conversations within the application. It establishes the structure for individual messages and the overall chat threads, linking them to user participants.

## Overview

The `chat.js` file is crucial for enabling communication between users. It exports the `Chat` Mongoose model, which encapsulates chat participants and their messages. This model is primarily consumed by chat-related routes and services, such as `src/routes/chat.js` and associated controllers, to handle creating, fetching, and updating chat conversations. It relies on the `User` model (`src/models/user.js`) for participant and sender references.

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Message Structure" icon="✉️">
    Defines the sender, content, and timestamps for each individual message within a chat conversation.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Chat Threads" icon="💬">
    Manages conversations between multiple participants and aggregates all their messages within a single thread.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## Chat Schema Fields

The `Chat` model is built upon `chatSchema`, which includes a nested `messageSchema` for message details. These fields define the structure of chat documents stored in your MongoDB database.

<Note>
  All fields marked as `required` must be provided when creating or updating a chat document.
  `ObjectId` fields refer to unique identifiers for other Mongoose documents, typically `User` models in this case.
</Note>

<ParamField name="participants" type="Array<ObjectId>" required>
  An array of `ObjectId`s representing the users involved in this chat conversation.
  Each `ObjectId` must reference an existing `User` document from `src/models/user.js`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField name="messages" type="Array<Object>">
  An array of message objects, each conforming to the `messageSchema`. This stores the conversation history.
  <Expandable title="Message Object Properties">
    <ParamField name="messages[].senderId" type="ObjectId" required>
      The `ObjectId` of the user who sent this particular message. Must reference an existing `User` document.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField name="messages[].text" type="string" required>
      The content of the message.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField name="messages[].createdAt" type="Date">
      Automatically generated timestamp for when the message was created. Managed by Mongoose `timestamps`.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField name="messages[].updatedAt" type="Date">
      Automatically generated timestamp for when the message was last updated. Managed by Mongoose `timestamps`.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<ParamField name="createdAt" type="Date">
  Automatically generated timestamp for when the chat conversation document was created.
</ParamField>

<ParamField name="updatedAt" type="Date">
  Automatically generated timestamp for when the chat conversation document was last updated.
</ParamField>

## Usage Example

Here's how to interact with the `Chat` model, demonstrating how to create a new chat, add messages, and retrieve a populated chat with user details.

<CodeGroup>
```javascript JavaScript
const { Chat } = require('../../src/models/chat');
const mongoose = require('mongoose');

// In a real application, these would be actual user IDs from your database
const userId1 = new mongoose.Types.ObjectId(); // Example User ID
const userId2 = new mongoose.Types.ObjectId(); // Example User ID

// Connect to MongoDB (ensure this is done once in your app)
// mongoose.connect('mongodb://localhost:27017/your_database', { useNewUrlParser: true, useUnifiedTopology: true });

/**
 * Creates a new chat conversation between two users.
 * @returns {Promise<Chat|null>} The newly created chat document or null on error.
 */
async function createNewChat() {
  try {
    const newChat = await Chat.create({
      participants: [userId1, userId2],
      messages: [
        { senderId: userId1, text: 'Hey there!' },
        { senderId: userId2, text: 'Hi! How are you?' }
      ]
    });
    console.log('New chat created:', newChat);
    return newChat;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error creating chat:', error.message);
    return null;
  }
}

/**
 * Adds a new message to an existing chat conversation.
 * @param {string} chatId - The ID of the chat to add the message to.
 * @param {string} senderId - The ID of the user sending the message.
 * @param {string} text - The content of the message.
 * @returns {Promise<Chat|null>} The updated chat document or null on error.
 */
async function addMessageToChat(chatId, senderId, text) {
  try {
    const updatedChat = await Chat.findByIdAndUpdate(
      chatId,
      {
        $push: { messages: { senderId, text } } // $push operator adds to array
      },
      { new: true, runValidators: true } // Return updated document and run schema validators
    );
    console.log('Message added to chat:', updatedChat);
    return updatedChat;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error adding message:', error.message);
    return null;
  }
}

// Example usage workflow:
(async () => {
  // 1. Create a chat
  const chat = await createNewChat();

  if (chat) {
    // 2. Add another message to that chat
    await addMessageToChat(chat._id, userId1, 'I am good, thanks!');

    // 3. Retrieve the chat and populate user details for display
    const populatedChat = await Chat.findById(chat._id)
                                    .populate('participants', 'email username') // Populate 'email' and 'username' fields from User model
                                    .populate('messages.senderId', 'email username'); // Populate sender details for each message
    
    console.log('\n--- Populated Chat Details ---');
    console.log(JSON.stringify(populatedChat, null, 2));
  } else {
    console.log('Failed to create chat, cannot proceed with further examples.');
  }

  // If you want to close the connection after examples
  // mongoose.disconnect();
})();
```
</CodeGroup>

<Info>
  The `.populate()` method is essential when fetching chat documents to retrieve actual user details (like `email` or `username`)
  instead of just their `ObjectId`s. This is because `participants` and `messages.senderId` fields are defined as references to the `User` model.
</Info>

## Common Errors / Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Mongoose Validation Error: Missing required fields">
    If you attempt to create a `Chat` document without providing all `required` fields (e.g., `participants` array, or `senderId`/`text` within a message object), Mongoose will throw a `ValidationError`.
    <Tip>
      Always ensure your request payload or direct `Chat.create()` call includes all necessary fields as defined in the schema. Check your server logs for specific validation messages from Mongoose, which will indicate exactly which field is missing or invalid.
    </Tip>
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="`CastError`: Invalid `ObjectId` format">
    If an `ObjectId` provided for a `participant` or `messages[].senderId` does not conform to a valid MongoDB 24-character hexadecimal `ObjectId` format, Mongoose will typically throw a `CastError`. This can happen if an ID is malformed or an incorrect type.
    <Check>
      Validate all `ObjectId`s using `mongoose.Types.ObjectId.isValid(id)` before attempting to use them in database operations to catch malformed IDs early.
    </Check>
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Populated fields return `null` or are empty">
    When using `.populate()`, if a referenced `User` `ObjectId` (e.g., for a participant or message sender) does not correspond to an existing document in the `User` collection, the populated field will appear as `null` or `undefined` instead of the expected user object.
    <Warning>
      Ensure that all `ObjectId`s stored in `participants` and `messages.senderId` genuinely refer to existing `User` documents in your database. This typically means checking the user creation and deletion logic to prevent orphaned references.
    </Warning>
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>
